title: No percolation at criticality on quasi-transitive graphs
main_claim: Take any infinite, connected, locally finite quasi-transitive graph with p_c < 1. Critical Bernoulli bond percolation on it has no infinite cluster almost surely. This would settle the bond case of the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture, and it includes Z^d for every d >= 2, so Z^3 too. The proof has three branches: Hutchcroft's theorem for exponential growth; for superpolynomial but subexponential growth, an entropy/interpolation argument that contradicts an adjacent-cluster bound of order s^{-1/2}; and for the polynomial-along-a-subsequence case, a nilpotent quotient (via Tessera–Tointon), induction, two approximate moves, a joint gluing inequality, and a corridor exploration that produces percolation below p_c.

issues.location: structure.tex, Prop. nilpotent-model (use of Tessera–Tointon Cor. 2.4)
issues.description: Two facts are taken from the cited corollary rather than proved here: the quotient Q = A/H has finite vertex stabilizers on Gamma/H, and H has finite-diameter orbits, for a transitive group A that is not assumed closed. The paper asserts that these hypotheses and conclusions match the cited statement. I could not check this against the source. The argument depends on it: finiteness of rho(Lambda_v) is what makes the equivariant projection pi well defined.
issues.evidence: "Its hypotheses require only one sufficiently large scale and do not require A to be closed ... The conclusion supplies a normal subgroup H whose orbits have finite diameter, such that Q=A/H ... has finite vertex stabilizers."

coverage:
I read all of the LaTeX (introduction, preliminaries, two-cluster-dfs-entropy, interpolation, superpolynomial, gluing, structure, moves, corridor-exploration, assembly) and checked these steps line by line:
- The AKN/ghost-field identity and the Doob bound that give P(H_s(e)) <= C s^{-1/2}, plus the averaging that passes to a single edge.
- Lemma dfs: the alpha/beta/gamma/sigma partition, both avoidance covariance inequalities, the Harris inequality u >= (u+v)(u+x), the tilted-martingale increment formula and the converted-budget chain.
- The entropy lemma, including the pooled Cauchy–Schwarz step and the shifted-Legendre endpoint bound.
- In the interpolation: contact normalization, the second moment, the density bound, the inverse-guess ratio, D_Omega <= 2L + J log 4, the decomposition D(Q||nu_i), and E_mu[W(1+W)] <= 4.
- In the superpolynomial theorem: band selection, the resampling argument for a nearby distinct large cluster, minimality of d, short connections at least theta^2/8, and the final o(log s) versus (1/2)log s contradiction.
- The joint gluing theorem: the deleted-set residual, the cluster-partition identity, column positivity, H^{-1} = I - Gamma and the row-mass identity. I also brute-forced the inequality on about 4500 random graphs with up to 8 vertices; the minimum gap was about -1e-13, which is floating-point rounding, not a counterexample.
- Fresh-collar transfer: the few-contacts shell bound, independence of the trial bits, the Harris+Markov step, and gluing applied after fixing xi.
- Corridor layout, the vertical-correction arithmetic, the stored-prediction and prospective-transfer logic, the conditional failure bound (at most epsilon) and the directed contour count.
- In Prop. moves: the Case 1 disk/winding argument, the strip-ray contradiction and the Case 2 construction.
- The induction on cyclic series and the bounded-projection lemma.

Not verified against the sources: the exact statements of Tessera–Tointon Cor. 2.4 and Hutchcroft 2016 Thm 1.2.
